postmortem.what_happened: J034 was the C08 mechanical long-peso position from the 18 Nov review (final forecast 51%), filled at the 19 Nov Banxico FIX and closed at the 20 Nov FIX when the 19 Nov review flipped the MXN forecast to 49%. The FIX barely moved between the two marks (about 0.02% in the peso's favour), even though the peso swung through the day on 19 Nov as global equities sold off and the dollar held near a 19-month high; costs left a net loss of about 0.007% of the account.
postmortem.assessment: A one-day holding cannot test a 20-trading-day thesis, so the result says nothing about the forecast; it will be judged when JF-series MXN forecasts resolve. The real decision to judge is the flip itself: moving from 51 to 49 on one day's news after the base mark had already absorbed it turned a near-even view into a round-trip cost for no information gain. With forecasts this close to 50, a one- or two-point change across 50 is noise, and C08 makes the book pay for it.
postmortem.do_differently: Treat a move across 50 by one or two points as needing new information that is not already in the base mark, not a re-reading of the same day's moves. When a forecast sits at 49-51, prefer keeping the previous side unless the evidence has clearly changed. Note that the 25% no-trade band does not protect against side flips, so near-even forecasts carry a cost each time they cross 50.
